Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Retrieve prior knowledge before revealing the method.
Talk track: Can the roadmap's conclusion stand in for our model output?
Expected answer / misconception: No. It motivates a workflow but does not provide our candidate's result or accuracy.
Visual: The three conditions identify what must be compared.

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: A public architecture reference and a classroom model output are different evidence types; keep their provenance separate. Trace the visual in order: public reference; course case ID; model revision. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: For the roadmap case, cite its chapter and page. For any InPack.AI demonstration, record the actual case ID and export revision; write 'not available' if absent.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R2: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 13: Co-Design | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch13_HIR_Co-Design.pdf
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: For the roadmap case, cite its chapter and page. For any InPack.AI demonstration, record the actual case ID and export revision; write 'not available' if absent. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. 
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: Hold use case, load, temperature, units, and output definition fixed before ranking layouts. Trace the visual in order: same requirement; same condition; comparable output. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Synthetic A and B differ only in memory placement. If A's temperature is reported at full power and B's at idle, refuse the comparison. Boundary: Candidate A/B is a synthetic teaching scenario, not InPack.AI output.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: A predicted peak or warpage remains a model result until checked against a suitable physical measurement. Trace the visual in order: input / model; predicted output; physical check. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: The public roadmap suggests co-design; a course run may predict a thermal difference. The design brief names what sensor, specimen, and condition would test it.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
